records.text:
perf(request): probe the body cache without allocating (#5176)

`#cachedBody` used `Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]` to find any already
cached body, allocating a fresh array on every body read (`req.json()`,
`req.text()`, ...) just to read one element.

A `for ... in` loop that returns on its first iteration gives the same
first-key-by-insertion-order result with no allocation. `bodyCache` is a
plain object literal, so there are no enumerable prototype keys to
consider.

records.text:
fix(request): keep the request media type when reusing a cached body (#5366)

* fix(request): keep the request media type when reusing a cached body

`HonoRequest` caches the parsed body so it can be read through more than one
representation. The fallback that rebuilds a body from an already cached
representation went through a bare `Response`:

    return new Response(body)[key]()

A `Response` constructed that way has no `Content-Type`, so a representation
that needs the media type could no longer be produced even though the bytes
were still available:

    app.post('/', async (c) => {
      const raw = await c.req.text()   // e.g. verify a signature first
      const form = await c.req.formData() // TypeError
    })

For an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data` request the
second call threw `TypeError: Content-Type was not one of ...`. `c.req.blob()`
was unaffected (a `Blob` carries its own type) and `c.req.parseBody()` was
unaffected (it reads the media type from `req.raw.headers`), so the same app
behaved differently depending on which accessor was used first.

Carry the original `Content-Type` over when rebuilding the body. `FormData` is
left alone, because `Response` has to generate a fresh multipart boundary for it.

* refactor(request): check the cache key instead of instanceof FormData
